Alex / Marta — feel free to add any constraints (SLA, on-call windows, blackout windows for retraining).

Thanks Ben — looping up a compact intake checklist below and I’ll follow with a calendar invite for a 30-min intake session. I attached a draft MOP and our proposed burst policy spreadsheet.

Proposed 10-point intake checklist (to be completed by Vertex during kickoff):
1) Primary region: us-west-2 (preferred) or us-east-1 — pick one + fallback region.
2) Peak profile: baseline 100–150 vGPU-hours/day; daily evening retrain window (00:00–06:00 PST) with spikes to 600 vGPU-hours.
3) IP allowlist / VPC peering details + CIDR ranges.
4) Data residency / encryption requirements (KMS/HSM).
5) Expected request QPS and 95th p90 token length (helps sizing batching).
6) Canary rollout policy (percentage over 72h).
7) Autoscale policy: min 2 instances, target latency 120–200ms p95, max burst nodes 8 for fast spin-up.
8) Fallback model variants (quantized) for low-cost fallback.
9) On-call rotation and escalation contact.
10) Blackout windows for maintenance / retrains.

Proposed timeline (2 weeks):
- Day 0–2: Intake session + finalize MOP items + obtain PO.
- Day 3–6: Network enablement (allowlist/VPC), template SOW sign-off.
- Day 7–10: Pool provisioning + config of autoscale and KV cache policies.
- Day 11–13: Canary traffic + observability thresholds + cost guardrails.
- Day 14: Cutover to production; 7-day monitoring window.

I’m attaching the MOP (vertex-mop-v1.pdf) and a draft burst policy (redwood-burst-policy-draft.xlsx). Alex/Marta — can you confirm the primary region and if you need an NDA amendment for on-prem data connectors?

Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
--
[Attachment: redwood-burst-policy-draft.xlsx (xlsx)]

Thanks Priya — this looks good and super-helpful. Quick answers from our side: 
- Primary region: us-east-1; fallback: us-west-2.
- IP allowlist: will provide CIDRs by EOD Monday.
- Data residency: standard AES-256; we will request KMS integration (company-wide KMS).
- Blackout: weekly rebuild window Friday 22:00–02:00 ET (we can align retrain).

A couple clarifying questions for the MOP and autoscale: 
1) How quickly can the burst nodes spin up? We need to guarantee capacity for scheduled retrains at 22:00 ET; cold start of nodes should be <12 minutes.
2) Can you set a cost-guard that automatically moves long-running low-priority jobs to a quantized fallback model?

Procurement (cc): we expect to sign the SOW this week — can you confirm PO number timeline?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Infrastructure
Vertex Analytics

Alex / Team—

Quick ops note after reviewing the MOP + burst draft: we can meet the <12 minute warm-up if we pre-warm a pool of standby instances using a fast-start profile (t2f-optimized). Proposed configuration:
- Standby pool: 2 pre-warmed nodes in fallback region (us-west-2) that can be promoted in ~3–6 minutes.
- Rapid burst nodes: ephemeral instances spun from a pre-built image with warmed KV cache snapshot; expected cold-start 10–12 minutes, warm-start 3–5 minutes.
- Autoscale policy changes: keep min instances at 2, target CPU/GPU utilization 45–65% with manual ramp to 80% allowed for scheduled retrains.
- Cost-guard: yes — we can implement an automated commuter that re-routes long-running, low-priority jobs to quantized variants with a configurable age threshold (default: 20 minutes).

Network / netops items we need from Vertex ops before provisioning:
- Exact CIDR list and any NAT/egress constraints.
- Any private peering/VPC endpoint requirements.
- Preferred SSH bastion IPs for debugging (if needed).

Priya — I’ll draft a short ops runbook snippet with the pre-warm script and the KV snapshot steps. Can we schedule a technical intake at 10:00 AM ET Monday to lock the CIDRs and PO?

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Implementation Engineer
Redwood Inference
